seo.title: Kovetz — merge JW Library backups and export your notes
seo.description: Free app for JW Library users (Jehovah's Witnesses): merge backups from all your devices and export notes to PDF or Obsidian. Android, Windows, Linux.
seo.tagline: Bring all your study notes into one backup.
seo.keywords: JW Library, JW Library backup, merge JW Library backups, JW Library notes, move JW Library notes to a new phone, JW Library notes to PDF, Obsidian, Jehovah's Witnesses, .jwlibrary, Android, Windows, Linux

ui.disclaimer: Kovetz is an independent program, not affiliated with JW Library or its developers.
ui.top: Back to the top of the guide

hero.title: All your JW Library notes — in one place
hero.text: Phone, tablet, computer: every device keeps its own notes. Kovetz merges your JW Library backups into one that you can restore in the app.
hero.alt: Kovetz screen showing a completed merge of JW Library backups

problem.title: Your study gems are scattered across devices
problem.text: As you read and study, different notes build up on your phone, tablet, and computer. Restoring a backup in JW Library replaces the notes on that device with the notes from that backup.
problem.diagramAlt: Kovetz brings backups from a phone, tablet, and computer into one file

solution.title: Kovetz brings your study notes together
solution.text: Add backups from different devices, even ones made years apart. Kovetz merges notes, highlights, bookmarks, favorites, and answers into a single .jwlibrary file.
points: If you edited a note in two places, the merged backup keeps the newer version and the report preserves the other.
You can restore the merged backup in JW Library on the device of your choice.

features.title: Keep your notes and read them where you like

cards.title: Keep your original backups
cards.text: Kovetz saves the result as a separate file and reports anything it could not transfer. Even backups from 2019 are supported.

cards.title: Read outside the app
cards.text: Save notes as a PDF book with a table of contents by tag and page numbers. Read it on screen or print it.

cards.title: Take your notes to Obsidian
cards.text: Get one Markdown file per note, index pages by tag, and internal links that are ready to use.

cards.title: Choose your backups
cards.text: Select “Choose files” and add backups from your phone, tablet, and computer.
cards.alt: Two JW Library backup files selected for merging

cards.title: Select “Merge”
cards.text: Review the merge rules. Kovetz reads your backups and combines them into one file.
cards.alt: Conflict resolution options for merging two backups

cards.title: Save the result
cards.text: Restore the merged file in JW Library, or choose “Export notes” and select PDF or Obsidian.
cards.alt: Export screen with choices for a PDF book or an Obsidian folder

pdf.title: PDF book
pdf.text: Find the right page using the table of contents by tag. Within each tag, sort notes by source or date. The PDF supports Cyrillic and Armenian text.
pdf.coverAlt: Cover of a PDF book of exported notes
pdf.pageAlt: Sample page from a PDF book with notes and a page number

obsidian.title: Obsidian folder
obsidian.text: Each note gets its own Markdown file with the source in its properties. Tag pages link to the matching notes, and the main index helps you find your way around.

privacy.title: Runs on your device
privacy.text: Your backups and notes are processed on your device. Kovetz connects to GitHub only if you choose to check for updates. You can use the app without an account.

guide.title: Easy to follow at any age
guide.text: The guide walks you through one step at a time, with large screenshots that show exactly where to click or tap. Read it on the site or print a copy.

support.title: Free, and always will be
support.text: One person builds Kovetz in his spare time. The app is free and ad-free. If it helped you, you can make an optional donation to support development or buy me a coffee.

name.title: Why “Kovetz”
name.text: “Kovetz” (קוֹבֶץ) is Hebrew for “collection”, “compilation” and also “file”. It comes from a root meaning “to gather”, which is exactly what the app does: it gathers your notes from different devices into one backup.

items.question: How do I merge JW Library notes from my phone and tablet?
items.answer: Make a backup in JW Library on each device, copy the .jwlibrary files to one device, add them to Kovetz and press “Merge”. Then restore the result in JW Library.

items.question: How do I move my JW Library notes to a new phone?
items.answer: Make a backup on the old phone and, if needed, merge it with the backups from your other devices in Kovetz. Then restore the resulting file on the new phone.

items.question: Does JW Library sync notes between devices officially?
items.answer: According to the help pages on jw.org, notes, tags, highlights and bookmarks are not synchronized between devices automatically. A backup can be restored on another device, but it replaces that device's data. Kovetz helps you merge backups.

items.question: My notes disappeared after restoring a backup. What can I do?
items.answer: Restoring in JW Library replaces the data on your device. If older backups still contain your notes, merge them with Kovetz and restore the combined file.

items.question: Do I need an internet connection?
items.answer: You only need it to download Kovetz and to check for updates if you choose. Merging and exporting work offline.

items.question: Is it safe for my original backups?
items.answer: Kovetz writes the result to a separate file and leaves your original backups untouched. Always make a fresh backup of your device before restoring.

items.question: What happens if I edit the same note on two devices?
items.answer: The merged backup keeps the newer version and saves the other version in the report.

items.question: Will notes I deleted come back?
items.answer: Yes, if a deleted note still exists in one of the backups you added to the merge.

items.question: Which backups can I use?
items.answer: Kovetz accepts .jwlibrary files from different devices, including backups made in different years.

items.question: Can I import notes back into JW Library from PDF or Obsidian?
items.answer: Restore the merged .jwlibrary backup to bring notes back into JW Library. PDF and Obsidian exports are for reading and searching.

items.question: How much does Kovetz cost?
items.answer: Kovetz is free. Its source code is available under the MIT license.

items.question: Is Kovetz an official JW Library app?
items.answer: Kovetz is an independent program, not affiliated with JW Library or its developers.

items.question: Does Kovetz work on Android?
items.answer: Yes. There is an APK installer for Android (arm64), which fits almost all modern phones and tablets. Versions for Windows 10 and 11 and for Linux are available too.

items.question: Is this a replacement for JWLMerge?
items.answer: You can use it as an alternative. Its author says JWLMerge has been unmaintained since 2023 and does not cover the new JW Library database schema. Kovetz works with backups from older and newer versions and also exports your notes.

items.question: Who is Kovetz for?
items.answer: For anyone who uses JW Library: Jehovah's Witnesses and interested people, as well as others who keep notes on more than one device.

audience.title: Who it is for
audience.text: Kovetz is made for people who study the Bible with the JW Library app: Jehovah's Witnesses, interested people and anyone who keeps notes, highlights and bookmarks on more than one device. Whether you prepare meeting parts, keep records for the ministry or collect findings from personal study, Kovetz gathers them into one backup and saves them as a PDF book or for Obsidian.
audience.note: Kovetz is an independent app and is not affiliated with JW Library or its developers.
